elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “Company and its affiliates,” although affiliate coverage is conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Contractors acting on Company's behalf are not expressly included as licensees. A right to grant sublicences permits, but does not itself provide, contractor coverage.
The licence is expressly perpetual and royalty-free, so any licence granted under this clause is perpetual.
The clause does not state that the licence is irrevocable or otherwise prohibit revocation.

elements.element: Subscription licences cannot be terminated for any reason other than material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is granted; the operative grant is expressly perpetual and royalty-free, so the condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is granted; the operative grant is expressly perpetual and royalty-free, so the condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to a successor in a merger or acquisition and does not cover successors arising through other transactions or by operation of law.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends to “Company and its affiliates (on written notice to Contractor).”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly “transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition without Contractor's approval.” This specific licence-transfer permission addresses the otherwise applicable consent restriction in Section 10.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the fallback by adding affiliate coverage subject to written notice and M&A-successor transferability. It does not reach the preferred position because contractors are not covered, irrevocability is omitted, and successor transferability is limited to merger or acquisition contexts. The changes are confined to the fallback requirements and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
